comments.author: trueIoV
comments.body:
Hi RichardAH, why not increase the number of signers to 100 in this case?
Especially since KAVA once stated that it could not integrate XRPL precisely because they need 100 signatures and no less.
Thanks.

comments.author: RichardAH
comments.body:
@trueIoV 128 is possible but there should be some debate about the "right" number. Too many is an attack vector as follows:
Suppose we allow 65536 signatures and someone continually submits txns with 65535 correct signatures and 1 incorrect signature at the end. The nodes they send these txns to have to check all 65536 signatures and then discard the txn without billing any account on-ledger. This vector could be mitigated in several ways, one of which is to allow a fee claim failure to occur on any multisig transaction with more than X correct signatures, where X is an absolute number not relative to the total.

## High Level Overview of Change
An amendment __ExpandedSignerList__, which if accepted, would:
1. Expand the maximum signer list to 32 entries
2. Allow the optional specification of 32 byte tags with each signer list entry



### Context of Change
The motivation for this amendment is two fold:
1. Large organisations may have extensive signer lists which require more than 8 keys and may benefit from tags (for example to identify who is in possession of each key.)
2. Layer two smart contract solutions such as Evernode-hotpocket, codius and others gain a security benefit for a common use-case: 
- Often it is useful for layer 2 contracts to control layer 1 accounts, from which they send and rec

reviewCommentsList.author: nbougalis
reviewCommentsList.body:
I understand why you want this field and concede that it's useful, but it may be slightly controversial in terms of size.

So is a 256-bit value _really_ needed? Could we get away with something smaller? I think your original suggestion was to use a 64-bit tag. I suspect that would be fine, but maybe a little too constrained for what you want to do. 128 bits is probably sufficient, especially if you use it as an [RFC-4122 UUID](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc4122) (likely V1, V4 or V5, depending on the usecase).

I am not _overly_ concerned and I think it's fine as is, but I do think it's worth at least having a discussion about this to ensure the field is "right-sized".
